AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 17, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Memo Parra
  Imago Dei Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Gavin Moore, 5th grader
  Paddison Elementary

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  1. City Council to proclaim National Public Works Week as May 15 - 21, 2022 in the City of Norwalk and
  share a video.

  2. Traffic Safety Awareness Art Contest under Special Presentations.
 CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Teen Alliance Scholarship and Recognition Dinner video.

  3.  Cinco de Mayo program video.

  4.  Department Highlights – Human Resources.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of May 3,
  2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period April 17, 2022 – April 30,
  2022, in the total amount of $962,245.03. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  26, through May 9, 2022 in the total amount of $4,277,858.43. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Andrew Heath.
  830-08

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – MAY 11, 2022 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  PROJECT NO. 7232 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND
  INSPECTION SERVICES FOR TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS ALONG ALONDRA
  BOULEVARD FROM HOME DEPOT DRIVEWAY TO SHOEMAKER AVENUE FEDERAL PROJECT
  NO. HSIPL-5347(042) – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with FCG Consultants,
  Inc., in an amount not-to-exceed $304,310 for construction management and inspection services for
  Project No. 7232, Traffic Signal Improvements on Alondra Boulevard from Home Depot Driveway to
  Shoemaker Avenue; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments,
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  1005-04-7232

  Report

  7.  PROJECT NO. 7233 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND
  INSPECTION SERVICES FOR INTELLIGENT TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS
  ALONG FIRESTONE BOULEVARD BETWEEN TARGET DRIVEWAY AND ROSECRANS AVENUE
  (FEDERAL PROJECT NO. HSIPL-5347(043)) – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement
  with Transtech Engineers, Inc., in an amount not-to-exceed $231,800 for construction management
  and inspection services for Project No. 7233, Intelligent Transportation System Improvements on
  Firestone Boulevard between the Target Driveway and Rosecrans Avenue and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7233
   Report

  8.  PROJECT NO. 7234 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND
  INSPECTION SERVICES FOR PROJECT NO. 7234 TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS ALONG
  STUDEBAKER ROAD BETWEEN KENNY STREET AND ROSECRANS AVENUE FEDERAL
  PROJECT NO. HSIPL-5347(044) - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with FCG
  Consultants, Inc., in an amount not-to-exceed $302,010 for construction management and inspection
  services for Project No. 7234, Traffic Signal Improvements on Studebaker Road between the Kenny
  Street and Rosecrans Avenue; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any
  amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 1005-04-7234

  Report

  9.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  10. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – MAY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

  11. REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR WORLD BOXING COUNCIL - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the boxing tournament requested by the World Boxing Council for
  the dates of Tuesday, June 14 through Monday, June 20, 2022 on the Civic Center lawn, and waive the
  security deposit as requested consistent with past practice. 920-01-02

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  13. FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT - The City Attorney
  recommends that the City Council approve the First Amendment to the City Manager’s Employment
  Agreement between the City of Norwalk and Jesus M. Gomez.

  Report

  14. ART IN PUBLIC PLACES PROJECT APPROVAL – COVID-19 MEMORIAL - Staff recommends City
  Council approve:

  a.  the COVID-19 memorial art piece, memorial ring, and additional site work; and

  b.  an agreement with James Naish Studio to design and build a COVID-19 art piece in an amount
  not-to-exceed $15,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing
  authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report
   15. NORWALK TRANSIT VILLAGE PROJECT UPDATE - CITY PROJECT NO. 7859 - Staff recommends
  City Council receive and file this report and provide feedback on the proposed project.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated May 12, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
